draft.title: Plant and animal cells compared
card: Plant cells and animal cells are both eukaryotic. Both have a nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes and a plasma membrane.
Cell wall
a rigid layer outside the plasma membrane of a plant cell. It supports the cell and gives it a fixed, regular shape. Animal cells have no cell wall.
Chloroplasts
found in the green parts of plants, where they carry out photosynthesis. Animal cells have no chloroplasts, so they cannot make food this way.
Large vacuole
a plant cell often has one large central vacuole that stores water and dissolved substances. Animal cells have no large central vacuole, though some have small ones.
draft.remember: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. Animal cells have none of these.

a.q: Which structure is found in a plant cell but not in an animal cell?
opts: A cell wall
A nucleus
A plasma membrane
A mitochondrion
a.why: A cell wall sits outside the plasma membrane of plant cells only. The nucleus, plasma membrane and mitochondria are found in both cell types, so they cannot tell the two apart.
a.clue: Both cell types are eukaryotic, so think of what only plants add.

b.q: A student views a cell under a microscope. It has a nucleus and mitochondria, but no cell wall, no chloroplasts and no large central vacuole. What can the student conclude?
opts: It is consistent with an animal cell
It must be a prokaryotic cell
It is consistent with a root cell of a plant
It cannot be a eukaryotic cell
b.why: A nucleus and mitochondria show the cell is eukaryotic. The missing cell wall, chloroplasts and large vacuole fit an animal cell. A plant root cell would still have a cell wall and a large vacuole, even without chloroplasts.
b.clue: Check which of the three plant features are absent, and whether the cell has a nucleus.

b.best: It is consistent with an animal cell

problems.detail: The remember line says flatly that plant cells have chloroplasts and a large vacuole. The card is more careful: chloroplasts are found only in the green parts of plants, and a plant cell 'often' has one large central vacuole. The remember line overstates this, and it clashes with question b's reasoning that a root cell has no chloroplasts.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and the card is accurate. The remember line overgeneralises: it says all plant cells have chloroplasts and a large vacuole, while the card limits chloroplasts to green parts and says the large vacuole is only 'often' present.
